To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
crack growth in a 304 stainless steel at high temperatures under mixed mode conditions is governed by the hydrostatic stress.

(1) the hydrostatic stress was the most accurate multiaxial damage parameter for predicting crack growth under mixed-mode conditions, (2) crack growth under mixed loading conditions is a function of both the maximum principal tensile stress and the hydro-static stress, and (3) crack growth in mode II loading is governed by the maximum effective stress.

the crack growth rates in 304 stainless steels are best correlated with the hydrostatic stress, and the angle of crack growth in 300 stainless steel is best correlated with a combination of the hydrostatic stress and maximum principal stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fracture criterion for high temperature crack growth.
understanding the mechanisms of high temperature crack growth and the factors that control the crack growth direction under mixed mode conditions.
the development of high temperature fracture mechanics data and the development of multiaxial fracture criteria for the design of high temperature structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high temperature crack growth is governed by the hydrostatic stress for mode I and mixed modes of loading, and is governed by the maximum effective stress for mode II loading.
the hydrostatic component of stress is the most important parameter in determining the direction of crack growth.
the hydrostatic component of stress is the most appropriate stress parameter for characterizing high temperature crack growth behavior in this material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crack growth rate is controlled by the hydrostatic stress and the angle of growth is controlled by the maximum principal stress.
a multiaxial damage mechanics approach is a promising approach for predicting high temperature fatigue crack growth in 316 stainless steel under mixed-mode loading conditions.
the hydrostatic tensile stress is the most important stress component for crack growth in 300 series stainless steels at temperatures above about 600 C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crack growth behavior under mixed mode conditions is governed by a combination of the maximum principal stress as well as the hydrostatic stress at the crack tip.
the damage mechanics approach can be used to predict crack growth rates under mixed mode loading.
crack growth is driven by the hydrostatic stress and the maximum principal stress.
